R and Stata side by side

Source: vignettes/articles/r-and-stata.Rmd
r-and-stata.Rmd

The R package is a port of the Stata command. Both fit the same models with the same formulas, and on the same data they agree to about seven significant digits: the R test suite compares the two on 29 specifications, covering every first stage, clustering, interaction effects, the bivariate probit, the three scales for the violation and the local-to-zero refits at Stata’s own draws.

The model

Stata R
apexog uci y x1 x2 (d = z1 z2) apexog(y ~ x1 + x2, endog = d ~ z1 + z2, method = "uci", ...)
apexog ltz ... method = "ltz"
(d1 d2 = z1 z2): shared instruments endog = d1 + d2 ~ z1 + z2
(d1 = z1 z2) (d2 = z2 z3): own instruments endog = list(d1 ~ z1 + z2, d2 ~ z2 + z3)
i.cat among the controls or instruments factor(cat)
(c.d c.d#c.x = z c.z#c.x): endogenous interaction endog = d + d:x ~ z + z:x
if x > 0 subset = x > 0
at least one control is needed y ~ 1 for a model without controls

(none) prior = function(n) ..., or draws = <matrix>

i.d / c.d prefix in the clause firststage = "probit" / "linear"
target(d1) target = "d1"
target(c.x#i.w) or aie(x w) aie = c("x", "w"), with aie_binary = c(FALSE, TRUE) to fix the types

Where the two differ

  • Random numbers. R and Stata draw different random numbers, so their local-to-zero intervals agree only up to simulation error. To reproduce a Stata run exactly, pass its draws: draws = <e(gamma_sim) as a matrix> (in latent units, the default gunits).
  • No controls. The Stata parser needs at least one exogenous control; R accepts y ~ 1.
  • Subsets with missing values. Observations where the subset expression is NA are dropped in R. Stata’s if treats a missing value as larger than any number and may keep them.
  • Factor variables. R’s model matrix drops base levels itself; Stata’s apexog removes base levels and collinear instrument terms before fitting. Both end with the same full-rank set of instruments.
  • An interaction already in the formula. With aie = c("x", "w") R uses a product x:w that the formula already contains (as in y ~ x * w); in Stata write the main effects only and let apexog add the product.
